notes: A completed request is decoded as a Receipt without status validation.
The text body is the successful return value even for an HTTP error.
A binary success path consumes an unchecked HTTP response.
Returning success after send is insufficient to establish successful HTTP status.
A long-lived broadcast subscription ends at the first lag error.
The ? propagates recoverable Lagged out of a continuing relay.
A wildcard receive failure terminates a broadcast loop.
The subscriber returns on lag without a fail-on-data-loss contract.
Dropping an owned JoinHandle does not stop the file-writing task.
An absolute deadline consumes the owned refresh handle; requests can continue after timeout.
The timeout error reports cancellation but the task is detached and still inserts rows.
A nested spawn future passed by value detaches after the timebox.
A tick cancels send and drops the popped job rather than retrying it.
The timeout drops the owned send payload; a retry counter is not a retained request.
Winning notification discards the current event and reads a different one.
The pause branch resumes the batch but the payload owned by the canceled send is gone.
Two independent defects in a catalog module: unchecked status and lag-stopped live updates.
The batch loses pending jobs on ticks and the separate deadline detaches its owned worker.
HTTP hard negative: error_for_status precedes success decoding.
HTTP hard negative: consuming an error body is deliberate after checking status.
HTTP hard negative and old_string trap: added code returns raw Response, removed code consumed unchecked JSON.
Broadcast hard negative: lag resynchronizes and the loop continues; only closure ends it.
Broadcast hard negative: explicit fail-on-data-loss policy intentionally terminates on lag.
Broadcast hard negative and MultiEdit old-string trap: only the removed code has a broadcast loop.
Timeout hard negative: retaining a mutable handle allows explicit abort and join.
Timeout hard negative and deleted-line trap: the added operation is an ordinary unspawned future.
Timeout hard negative: an owned handle is deliberately detached after a bounded wait.
Send hard negative: reserve is raced while the update remains outside the future. Context-only unsafe code must be ignored.
Send hard negative: the single pinned future survives every heartbeat branch.
Send hard negative: cancellation drops only a clone and retains the original for retry.
